description_full: International General Insurance Holdings Ltd. engages in the provision of specialty insurance and reinsurance solutions in the United Kingdom, Europe, Central and South America, the Middle East and Africa. The company operates through three segments: Specialty Long-tail, Specialty Short-tail, and Reinsurance. It is involved in underwriting a portfolio of specialty risks, including energy, property, construction and engineering, ports and terminals, general aviation, political violence, professional lines, financial institutions, marine, and treaty reinsurance. The company was founded in 2001 and is based in Amman, Jordan.

financial_summary: International General Insurance is a small-cap financial services business with a $996M market cap on $517M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are expanding by +48.9pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 25% against a 7% cost of capital — a 18-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $107M in free cash flow — roughly 21 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.85× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 10.9% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 42% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
